Russell Kent wrote 'What Did the Parkland Doctors Really Say?' for JFK Lancer, a research publisher. His subject is the doctors at Parkland Hospital who treated President Kennedy. Kent asks whether those doctors modified their descriptions of Kennedy's head injuries in later interviews.

The Parkland doctors' first accounts, given at a press conference that afternoon, described wounds in terms that later testimony seemed to soften. That difference has fueled argument for sixty years. Kent compares the early words with the later ones. His article is a study in how testimony drifts, and in why the first day's record matters to everyone who argues about the shooting.
the-life-of-marie-de-medicis-queen-of-fr: Julia Pardoe wrote her life of Marie de Medicis, consort of Henry IV and regent under Louis XIII, in three volumes issued in 1890. Only the title page, dedication, and the start of the contents are present here for volume one. Book one, on Marie as queen, opens with a chapter covering 1572 to 1599. Pardoe other court histories named on the page cover Louis XIV and Francis the First. The biography itself cannot be read in this record.
the-vision-of-hell-by-dante-alighieri-tr: Dante Alighieri's Vision of Hell, the Inferno, appears here in the English translation by the Reverend H. F. Cary, with illustrations by Gustave Doré. The pages present give the title and a list of cantos, so the poem itself does not appear. Thirty-four cantos are numbered in sequence, matching the full count of Dante's Hell. A heading for canto one follows the list, with no verse beneath it in what is preserved. Readers can identify the edition, its translator, and its illustrator from this record alone.
